state.goal: Find a strong free compiler lecture series on YouTube

found.text:
Crafting Interpreters is the official free online book by Robert Nystrom. It teaches two Lox interpreters: a Java tree-walk interpreter and a C bytecode virtual machine. The contents page lists all chapters, including the bytecode compiler and VM section. ([craftinginterpreters.com](https://craftinginterpreters.com/))
Sources:
[s1] Crafting Interpreters — https://craftinginterpreters.com/

A strong match is Douglas Thain’s Introduction to Compilers and Language Design, a free online textbook from the University of Notre Dame. It walks through building a compiler and includes chapters on parsing and code generation, plus example code. ([dthain.github.io](https://dthain.github.io/books/compiler/))

Another option is Compiler Construction: Fundamentals and Applications, hosted by Johannes Kepler University Linz. It covers syntax analysis, semantic processing, and code generation, with a MicroJava compiler example. ([ssw.jku.at](https://ssw.jku.at/CompilerBook/))
Sources:
[s2] Introduction to Compilers and Language Design | Prof. Douglas Thain at Notre Dame — https://dthain.github.io/books/compiler/
[s3] Compiler Construction - Fundamentals and Applications — https://ssw.jku.at/CompilerBook/

MIT OCW’s best match is 6.035, Computer Language Engineering. It includes lecture notes, problem sets, and five compiler-design projects. ([ocw.mit.edu](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-035-computer-language-engineering-sma-5502-fall-2005/pages/projects/))

For a shorter introduction, see the compiler material in 6.004, Computation Structures. ([ocw.mit.edu](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c11/))
Sources:
[s4] Projects | Computer Language Engineering (SMA 5502) | Electrical Engineering and Computer  — https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-035-computer-language-engineering-sma-5502-fall-2005/pages/projects/
[s5] 11 Compilers | Computation Structures | Electrical Engineering and Computer Science | MIT  — https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-004-computation-structures-spring-2017/pages/c11/
